title: Surface sheen overlay & data-ink preservation for branded dark themes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Several brand-enabled dark themes introduce subtle hue shifts and heavy brand tints that reduce the perceived contrast of data ink (table text, chart strokes, sparklines). In dense UIs (tables, small charts) this causes a drop in legibility and increases cognitive load for users. Goals: 1) Define a token layer that preserves ‘data-ink’ contrast across brand theme overlays without derailing brand color intent. 2) Introduce a lightweight ‘surface sheen’ token that provides a consistent micro-layer (subtle gradient or luminosity mask) for panels that aligns with brand accents without lowering text/line contrast. 3) Provide component override patterns for tables/charts/avatars that explicitly opt out of brand tinting when necessary (data-ink forced neutralization). 4) Ship design tokens, documented usage patterns, and a test harness for QA and accessibility checks.
acceptance_criteria: Token: data-ink-primary and data-ink-secondary defined with clear contrast targets (WCAG AA minimum against surface tokens) for all brand themes.
Token: surface-sheen defined as three presets (none, subtle, elevated) with CSS variables and Figma styles.
Component overrides: Table row text, table header sort icons, and chart stroke tokens can opt into data-ink-neutral to avoid brand tinting.
Design system usage docs added to Console Theming page with code examples (JS + CSS vars) and Figma token mapping.
Automated visual regression tests added (Chromatic/Storybook) for table and chart permutations across 4 brand themes and 2 density settings.
Accessibility checks added: color contrast report for all permutations showing AA compliance for primary flows.
Cross-team review: PM and Engineering sign-off and a follow-up engineering spike scheduled for runtime token mapping logic.
engineering_notes: Proposed implementation: add CSS vars --rwd-data-ink-primary / --rwd-data-ink-secondary and --rwd-surface-sheen-{none|subtle|elevated}. Runtime mapping will compute data-ink tokens by applying a perceptual desaturate + contrast-boost step against the themed surface background. Engineering to evaluate cost of runtime computation vs precomputed variants per brand. See PR template in comments for implementation constraints.
